w:r.w:t: KAVACH
A Secure National Examination Protocol
Simple Explanation of What We Are Building and How It Works
The Core Idea in One Sentence:

A readable question paper must never exist except for a very short, tightly controlled time window — right in front of an authenticated student or an authenticated printer — and every single action that touches the paper must leave a permanent, unchangeable digital record that no one can deny.
1. What Problem Are We Solving?

In India, high-stakes exams like NEET, JEE, board exams and government recruitment tests keep getting hit by paper leaks. These leaks destroy trust, force re-exams for millions of students, waste huge amounts of money, and cause enormous stress.

The real problem is not weak locks or weak encryption alone. The biggest risk is human trust. Someone who is authorised to see the final paper (a paper setter, a press worker, a transport official, or a centre staff member) can leak it. Traditional systems try to stop this with better seals, more police escorts, CCTV and stricter rules. But rules can be broken. We need a system where leaking the paper becomes mathematically extremely hard, not just against the rules.
2. What is KAVACH?
KAVACH (meaning “armour” or “shield”) is a complete software-based security system for examinations. It combines modern cryptography, a special kind of blockchain, and smart process design so that:
A complete readable question paper does not exist until just minutes before the exam starts.
No single person or single organisation can ever unlock the paper alone.
Every action (who did what, when, where, on which device) is permanently recorded in a way that cannot be changed or denied later.
The same system works for Computer-Based Tests (CBT), Just-in-Time Printing at centres, and even traditional pen-and-paper exams.
3. Core Design Principles (Simple Version)
No single point of trust:
It must never be possible for one person to see or release the full paper by themselves.
The paper is only a digital locked box:
Until the right moment, the paper exists only as encrypted data (scrambled text that no one can read).
Two keys are needed at the same time:
A time condition (the exam must be about to start) AND approval from several independent people/organisations.
Everything is recorded permanently:
If an action is not written on the special blockchain ledger, it is treated as if it never happened.
Software first:
We avoid the need for expensive special hardware boxes at every exam centre. We use cryptography and multi-party control instead.
4. How the System Works — Step by Step
Step A: Building the Question Bank (Safely)

Subject experts write individual questions, not full papers. Each question is encrypted as soon as it is submitted. Different experts work on different parts so that no one person ever sees a complete final paper. An AI tool checks for duplicate or very similar questions and blocks them. This solves the biggest traditional weakness: a paper setter leaking the whole paper.
Step B: Creating the Final Paper (Without Anyone Seeing It)

A computer program (not a human) selects questions according to a pre-approved blueprint (how many questions from each chapter, difficulty mix, etc.). The program creates a unique digital fingerprint (hash) of the paper and locks the entire paper with strong encryption. The decryption key is immediately broken into several pieces (using a technique called Shamir’s Secret Sharing) and given to different independent organisations (for example: exam board, education ministry, an independent observer, a state representative, a technical auditor). No single organisation holds the full key.
Step C: The Double-Gate Unlock (The Heart of the System)
To unlock the paper, two conditions must both be true at the same time (enforced by smart contracts on the blockchain):
Gate 1 – Time:
The official exam start time must have arrived (or be only a few minutes away).
Gate 2 – Quorum:
A minimum number of the independent key holders (for example 4 out of 7) must digitally approve the release from their own separate devices.

Only when both gates open does the system allow the encrypted paper to be decrypted — and only inside a temporary, tightly controlled process that is destroyed immediately afterwards. Before that moment, it is mathematically impossible to produce a readable paper.
Step D: Delivering the Paper to Centres or Students
Three modes use the exact same security backbone:
Computer-Based Test (CBT):

The encrypted paper sits on a secure server. When the student authenticates (biometric + other checks) and the double-gate opens, the paper appears only on the student’s screen for the duration of the exam and is wiped afterwards.
Just-in-Time Printing (JITP):

Minutes before the exam, authorised centre officials (always two people together) request unlock. The double-gate opens, the paper is decrypted only in the printer’s temporary memory, unique watermarked copies are printed, and the key is immediately destroyed. Every print is logged.
Traditional Pen-and-Paper (transition period):
The same cryptographic locks and blockchain records wrap the existing physical transport and storage process, so every checkpoint becomes a permanent digital record.
Step E: Watermarking and Tracing Leaks

Every printed page or screen display gets a unique invisible digital watermark that records the centre, the exact time, and the session. If a photo of a leaked paper appears on social media or messaging apps, forensic software can read the watermark and identify exactly which copy was leaked and from which centre — within minutes instead of weeks.
Step F: After the Exam – Answer Sheets (OMR)

OMR sheets are issued only to present candidates. Every scanned answer sheet is immediately given a digital fingerprint (hash) and recorded on the blockchain. Any later substitution or tampering becomes mathematically visible. The same secure chain-of-custody continues until results are published.
5. Key Technologies Used (Explained Simply)
AES-256-GCM Encryption:
Military-grade scrambling of the question paper so that without the key it is unreadable.
Shamir’s Secret Sharing (Threshold Cryptography):
The decryption key is split into several pieces. A minimum number of pieces must come together to reconstruct the key. One piece alone is useless.
Permissioned Blockchain (Hyperledger Fabric style):
A shared, permanent digital ledger run by several independent organisations. No single organisation can change or delete history. Every important action is written here as a permanent record.
Smart Contracts / Chaincode:
Rules written in code that automatically enforce the double-gate (time + multi-party approval). Illegal actions are simply rejected by the system.
Digital Signatures & PKI:
Every person and device signs their actions with a unique digital signature so they cannot later deny involvement.
Steganographic Watermarking:
Invisible digital marks hidden inside every printed or displayed page for later tracing.
AI Similarity Detection:
Automatically finds and blocks duplicate or reworded questions in the bank.
6. What Happens If Something Goes Wrong?
The system has a controlled emergency process (not a single “panic button”). If a leak is suspected:
The affected paper is marked as compromised (this itself needs multi-party approval).
All access to that paper is immediately revoked.
A fresh, equivalent paper is generated from the unused part of the question bank.

Only the affected centres receive the new paper. The rest of the country continues normally. This avoids the current painful situation of cancelling an exam for millions of students because of a localised leak.
7. Why This Approach Is Stronger
It does not rely only on people following rules — the mathematics itself prevents early unlocking.
No single insider (even a very senior one) can leak the final paper alone.
Every action creates permanent, court-usable evidence.
It works for both digital and paper-based exams under one architecture.
It can isolate a leak to a small area instead of forcing a national re-exam.
It is designed as software-first, so it can be rolled out without buying expensive special hardware for every single centre.
8. What We Are Building First (The MVP)
In the next one week our team will build a working demonstration (MVP) that shows the complete flow for a small number of candidates and centres. The demo will prove that:
A paper stays locked until both the time gate and the multi-party approval gate open.
Attempts to unlock early or with too few approvals are automatically rejected by the system.
Both CBT delivery and Just-in-Time Printing work under the same security rules.
A leaked page can be traced back to the exact centre and time via its watermark.
A complete, unchangeable audit trail of the entire lifecycle is available.
9. Final Thought

KAVACH does not claim that human beings will suddenly become perfect. It accepts that some people will try to leak papers. Its strength is that it makes successful, undetectable leaks extremely difficult, turns every action into permanent evidence, and allows the system to recover quickly without punishing millions of honest students.
In short: we are building a system where the question paper is protected by mathematics and multi-party control rather than by hope and human trust alone.
